# Volume 5 — CHAPTER XXXV. “LET THE PIPER COME”

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“And so,” Miss Winifred stated, “the two couples will be married at some point near the middle of this month.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0000 }

A slight coldness hung in the air during the early September evening, which led Nell to ignite her constantly prepared driftwood fire inside the large living room, where she and Miss Winifred took comfort in its magical glow.
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0001 }

“Particularly concerning Mr. Ashdown and Clementine, it is truly wonderful,” Nell remarked. “Thinking about it makes me just as joyful as I felt during my own wedding. Up on the hill yesterday night while I examined Clementine’s trousseau, I experienced the precise sensation of being a bride once more.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0002 }

“It has been mentioned to me that what she owns would suit a princess,” stated Tabitha out of a dark nook in which she held her brown boy close. “I was asked to go up and look at the items too, a trip I plan to make one night. Word has reached me that Clementine plans to wear a veil and white silk, whereas navy blue is chosen for Harriet's wedding. Mrs. Dr. dear, I do not question that her decision is quite practical, yet personally I have constantly held the opinion that should I ever get wed, I would choose the veil and white to feel more like a bride.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0003 }

An image of Tabitha dressed in “white and a veil” appeared to the mind’s eye of Nell, nearly overwhelming her.
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0004 }

“Regarding Mr. Ashdown,” Miss Winifred remarked, “his upcoming marriage alone has transformed him completely. Trust me, his dreaminess and preoccupation have been reduced by half. It was such a comfort to learn he had chosen to lock up the manse and allow the youngsters to stay with various people during his wedding trip. Had he permitted them and elderly Aunt Martha to remain in the house by themselves for four weeks, I would have anticipated waking up each day to find the building reduced to ashes.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0005 }

“Aunt Martha and Tobias will be arriving,” declared Nell. “Rupert’s destination is Elder Clow’s house. Their plans for the girls remain unknown to me.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0006 }

“Oh, I’m going to take them,” said Miss Winifred. “Naturally, I was happy to, though Mary would have bothered me endlessly until I asked them regardless. The manse will be cleaned from top to bottom by the Ladies’ Aid before the bride and groom return, and the cellar will be filled with vegetables through Lionel Fairlie's arrangements. Believe me, nobody has ever seen or heard anything remotely like Lionel Fairlie lately. Having desired Harriet Ainslie all his life, he is so thrilled that he is finally going to marry her. If I were Harriet—however, I’m not, and if it contents her, it can certainly content me. Years ago, when she was a schoolgirl, I overheard her state that a tame puppy was not what she wanted in a husband. Believe me, there’s nothing tame about Lionel.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0007 }

As dusk arrived above Fern Hollow, the pond sported a marvellous expanse of green, purple, crimson, and gold. Resting upon the eastern hill was a light blue mist, above which an enormous, round, pale moon was simply drifting upward in the manner of a silver bubble.
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0008 }

Every one of them was present, crouching in the small uncovered clearing—Grace and Ida, Tobias and Rupert, Kit and Edmund, Bess and Izzy, and Mary Stubbs. A particular party had been underway, because it was going to be the final night Kit spent in Fern Hollow. The next day he was set to depart for Port Marlow so he could go to Regent’s Academy. The group’s spellbound ring was going to be shattered; and, regardless of the lightheartedness of their small gathering, a trace of grief existed within each cheerful youthful soul.
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0009 }

“Look—over there in the sunset stands a massive golden palace,” Edmund said, pointing. “Gaze upon the gleaming tower—and the crimson banners floating from them. Maybe a victor returns home from war—and they hang them outside in his honour.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0010 }

“Oh, how I desire the return of the past,” Kit cried out. “It would be wonderful to serve as a soldier—to be a famous, victorious general. For the chance to witness a grand battle, I would sacrifice all I possess.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0011 }

Well, Kit was slated to enter the military and experience a fight larger than any previous one on earth; however, that remained a long time away; meanwhile, his mother, to whom he was the eldest boy, used to gaze at her sons while expressing gratitude to God that those “brave days of old” desired by Kit had ended permanently, meaning Canadian sons would not ever have to gallop away to war “for the ashes of their fathers and the temples of their gods.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0012 }

No icy harbinger of the Great Conflict's shadow had been experienced as of yet. Schoolboys, full of mischief and anticipating a good future, were what the young men who would do battle, and maybe perish, in the landscapes of France and Flanders, Gallipoli and Palestine then were; lovely young girls, glowing with expectations and fantasies, were what the young women whose spirits would be broken then were.
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0013 }

Gradually, the crimson and gold of the sunset city's banners were surrendered, and the conqueror’s pageant vanished at a slow pace. As twilight slid across the valley, silence descended upon the small gathered group. Edmund, who had spent time reading from his treasured book of myths earlier that day, recalled a former notion he had held about the Pied Piper descending into the valley during a dusk precisely such as this one.
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0014 }

He commenced speaking in a dreamy manner, in part due to his desire to give his companions a small thrill, and in part because an entity distinct from himself appeared to be utilizing his lips to speak.
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0015 }

“The Piper is drawing closer,” he said, “he is closer than he was on the evening I previously saw him. He has his long, shadowy cloak blowing about him. He pipes—he pipes—and we are forced to follow—Kit and Rupert and Tobias and I—around and around the globe. Listen—listen—are you unable to hear his wild music?”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0016 }

A shudder passed through the girls.
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0017 }

“You are fully aware that you are merely playing a part,” Mary Stubbs objected, “and I would prefer that you stopped. Your performance is far too convincing. That ancient Piper of yours is something I despise.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0018 }

However, laughing merrily, Kit leaped to his feet. Upon a small mound he stood, magnificent and lofty, possessing an unclouded forehead alongside his brave gaze. Throughout the country of the maple, there existed thousands similar to him.
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0019 }

“May the Piper arrive and be welcomed,” he exclaimed, making a gesture with his hand. “With joy, I will pursue him all over the earth.”
{: #nw-v05-c35-p0020 }
